subject: the harder problem after quality
text:
Hi [NAME],

Congrats on the cinematic outputs from Seedance 2.0!

Generation quality is table stakes now. The harder problem we've seen is that aesthetics and contextual cues that resonate with one user segment can be completely different from another (ads creator vs. filmmaker; American vs. Chinese markets, etc.)

We help video generation teams like Synthesia, Flawless and Tavus navigate this - improving diversity of human feedback and automating annotation, evaluation and QA review workflows. The objective is richer fine-tuning data: time-aligned audio-visual datasets for SFT and multi-dimensional preference signals for RLHF.

How are you thinking about output alignment at [COMPANY]? Worth a quick chat?

subject: Content moderation at scale
text:
Hi [NAME],

We just onboarded a brand safety team, helping them scale
auto-classification across markets. The main challenge was to understand
which model configuration performs best at automating manual moderation at
scale, while accounting for regional policy variation and
contextually-dependent content cues.

Here's how we're approaching it at Encord: we've built out a platform to
orchestrate model configuration (prompt + LLM/VLM/OCR pairing), model
performance evaluation and human labelling and verification in one place.

Would you be open to exchange perspectives on how you're navigating this?

subject: GenAI eval
text:
Hi [NAME], 

      Saw your work spanning booking, post-booking, and servicing - I imagine that means juggling multiple GenAI + predictive workflows, each with very different data quality and failure modes. 

      One common challenge we see across F500 and digital-native teams: GenAI performance ultimately depends on structured human feedback for evaluation. 

      That's where Encord fits - supporting preference ranking, pairwise comparisons, rubric-based eval across modalities, and curating eval sets around real failure modes. 

      Curious if this resonates on your side? Happy to compare notes in a quick 20-min intro chat.

subject: Synthesia's Multimodal data management solution
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently released EMM-1
<[LINK]>
 - the world's largest open-source multimodal dataset, with 107 million
image, video, text, audio and point cloud embeddings - and thought it might
be relevant given the work you're doing building Instant Diffusion from
scratch. The push into enterprise is exactly the kind of expansion we tend
to help to accelerate.

Our engineering team has been building out dataset curation and label
validation tooling specifically for visual AI teams at this stage of scale
- we're working with teams like Synthesia and would love to get your take
on what we've shipped.

Would you be open to a quick 15-minute chat to take a look, see if there's
any overlap, and share some honest feedback?
